findings.evidence: template/scripts/project_sync.py:40–48 reads HEAD, merges, reads HEAD again and writes an actor receipt without holding serialized_integration. If a delegated child advances integration from A to origin/main B after a sibling sync reads A, the sibling's merge succeeds as an 'Already up to date' no-op and emits A→B naming the sibling. The receipt then passes delegation_containment.py's chain and actor checks despite the child having moved integration. Two legitimate concurrent syncs can likewise emit duplicate A→B receipts and break the chain. The receipt append lock does not protect the HEAD observation and merge.
findings.summary: Unserialized project sync can attribute another process's integration advance to the caller, defeating detection-only containment.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/delegation_containment.py:434 reads the whole log with read_text().splitlines(), and read_integration_advances parses every entry before _receipt_chain filters by delegation time. Consequently memory and classification cost grow with all historical advances, despite design.md describing 'bounded reading by time window' as the mitigation for receipt log growth.
findings.summary: Every classification loads and parses the entire append-only integration history.
